Unequal detail is itself a comparison gap. Develop only the smallest missing fragment needed to compare the same task, output, conditions, support, and resource coordinates. Do not require complete competing courses when one closed task family can discriminate the alternatives.

#### HCD.2:4.4 - Compare the Finite Programme Changes

Use `C.11.CRC` to compare each realizable candidate configuration with the person's current configuration. Name the baseline, finite addition or substitution, candidate configuration, horizon, scenarios, result and resource coordinates, interactions, uncertainty, transition, reversibility, and option effects.

For HCD.2, the decision-bearing coordinates normally include:

- closure of the required later-Work outputs and protected critical-error conditions;
- learner, teacher, assessor, specialist, tool, and transition burden;
- dependence on references, AI, cues, project access, authority, and provider availability;
- preservation of current strengths and practice needed by other contributions;
- the qualified expectation and evidence plan for supported, independent, changed-condition, transfer, and delayed performance; and
- future development options and the cost of reopening a closed route.

Use `dominated`, `non-dominated`, `beneficial`, `harmful`, or `indeterminate` only for the candidates, coordinates, horizon, conditions, and evidence actually compared. A programme is not non-dominated merely because it was generated, and one feasible candidate is not dominant merely because no rival is ready. HCD.2 supplies the comparison claim; `C.11` supplies any later bounded choice from the complete choice inputs.

#### HCD.2:4.5 - Return the Programme-Comparison Account

Return one account containing:

| Result position | Required content |
| --- | --- |
| comparison boundary | Holder, later Work, supplied development stake, decision owner, candidates, horizon, conditions, participation, evidence window, and direct outside owners. |
| candidate descriptions | The comparable positions in §4.3 for every actual candidate, including any one candidate that remains feasible. |
| comparison claims | Supported relative contribution, burden, dependence, uncertainty, displacement, and option claims; any dominance relation is explicitly bounded. |
| access allocations | Intended human, reference, AI, specialist, provider, environment, permission, and timing contributions, with actual availability distinguished from assumption. |
| evidence and gaps | Sources and observations supporting each claim, missing values, unsupported stronger claims, and the conclusion each gap blocks. |
| disposition | `comparable candidates`, `one feasible candidate with comparison gap`, `current candidate set infeasible`, `personal comparison blocked with the exact missing input and its receiving owner`, or `learning-product design return for an unknown audience`. These are readable HCD.2 dispositions, not a final programme choice. |
| continuation | The smallest comparable fragment, provider result, personal observation, budget change, target decision, or other condition that permits the next comparison or choice. |

When a final choice is requested, pass this account to the authorized decision owner and the applicable decision Method. Preserve the option set, preferences, belief state, outcome model, protected conditions, probe worth, and authority required there. Do not turn the HCD.2 comparison into authorization, commitment, launch, or proof of effect.

#### HCD.2:4.6 - Recognition and Assurance

**Recognition.** Use HCD.2 when the live question sounds like “Which way could this person become able to do the whole job?” and the alternatives differ in preparation, practice, support, time, or future options. The smallest useful result may be one comparable task fragment rather than a complete curriculum.

**Assurance.** Stronger reliance needs same-holder and condition-compatible inputs, qualified target-domain tasks and error criteria, credible provider and access claims, complete resource coordinates, and explicit evidence limits. A programme can be compared before it is chosen or run. Effectiveness, transfer, retention, provider operation, and personal development require their own observations.

#### HCD.2:4.7 - What Changes in Practice

A practitioner stops asking, “Which course covers all the topics?” and asks, “Which finite programme change closes this person's complete later-Work tasks, with what human and external contributions, at what burden, and what evidence is still missing?” A detailed course becomes one candidate; an unknown audience receives a design question rather than an invented personal profile.

### HCD.2:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### HCD.2:5.1 - Constructed Personal Case: Learner-FP6

`Learner-FP6` is a constructed pedagogical holder. The stipulated entry attempt shows that this person can build a device model but confuses a flow unit, the recipient of the result, and the organizational permission needed for the proposed action. The intended later-Work outputs, mandatory tasks, 340 learner-hour limit, available teacher and worked examples, and protected critical errors are held fixed for this comparison. No observation of actual learning is claimed.

Two six-hour candidates replace harder optional cases rather than add time:

| Candidate | Finite change and intended contribution | Burden, dependence, and evidence gap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| focused preparation | Allocate two hours to selecting the result recipient, two to checking the required organizational permission and tracing consequences for other systems, and two to checking flow units and constraints before the next whole task. The mandatory tasks, later variation, and final result remain unchanged. | Uses an explicit prerequisite route and keeps teacher feedback inside the existing arrangement. It may isolate the three weaknesses clearly, but the comparison still needs a changed-condition whole-task attempt to show whether the contributions combine. |
| supported whole-task preparation | Use the same six learner hours for a complete decision task in which the person must calculate with the flow unit, address the right recipient, and obtain or respect the required permission. A worked example and bounded teacher questions support the first attempt; a changed case then removes answer-revealing help. | Tests integration earlier but may conceal which prerequisite failed. Selecting, demonstrating, and reviewing the extra case consumes teacher preparation and feedback Work that must fit an established capacity or be priced separately. |

HCD.2 returns two comparable descriptions, the common output and evidence plan, and the unresolved provider-load and changed-condition evidence. It does not choose between them. An independent attempt showing three separable errors would strengthen focused preparation; success on the components but failure to combine them would strengthen the whole-task candidate. Either observation reopens only the affected comparison claims.

#### HCD.2:5.2 - Unknown Audience: FoundationsProgramme A, B, and C

A learning-product author has two intended outcomes: checked performance of complete selected work tasks, and lower effort to learn a previously untaught Method while preserving correctness. These are design aims, not observed gains. The author has an audience hypothesis, three 340-hour compositions, and no named learners. A allocates 202/96/42 hours to general/domain/joint application, B allocates 88/204/48, and C allocates 136/136/68. C is described in more detail; that detail does not establish dominance.

The HCD.2 boundary returns a learning-product design question to HCD.28: preserve the two outputs, audience assumptions, three alternatives, learner and teacher resource coordinates, support assumptions, and individualization questions. Use C's existing material and develop only the smallest missing A/B fragment for one closed task family with the same output, entry assumptions, representative attempt, feedback, retry, access, and resource account. Do not fabricate one future learner or require three complete courses before comparison becomes useful.

If the learner budget falls from 340 to 204 hours while both outputs remain fixed, none of the three original candidates is launchable as described. Multiplying every activity by 0.6 or hiding reading and practice outside the budget does not close the task. The return asks for a new candidate that identifies the removed or replaced 136 hours and preserves the mechanisms needed for the outputs. The separate 240-hour teacher calculation does not replace learner time or establish a competent available service. A 170-hour ThinkingFoundations-only offer answers a narrower output question and therefore is not an improved version of the same candidate set.

#### HCD.2:5.3 - One Feasible Candidate Is Not a Winner

A named person has a qualified near-term engineering task and strong entry evidence. Only one candidate currently fits the deadline and available project access; a second candidate depends on an unavailable specialist. HCD.2 may return the feasible candidate, its finite comparison with the current configuration, and the exact specialist result that blocks the other candidate. It does not invent a weak rival, call the feasible programme universally best, or infer that the programme will work. A later provider result, deadline change, or changed task reopens the bounded comparison.

#### HCD.2:5.4 - Two Unfinished Lines and an Attractive New Start

In this constructed case, Lena has six learner-hours and two 45-minute sessions with a suitably qualified teacher in the coming week. The sessions can each return feedback early enough for a learner correction and subsequent check. The programme must preserve preparation for Friday's report. A second line concerns work next month; a simulation method might open a further project option.

Recover the remaining contribution of each line:

| Line | Existing evidence and remaining useful result | Remaining burden in this window |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A — justify a dashboard anomaly | Lena computes the indicator correctly. She still needs to distinguish two plausible explanations, select a discriminating observation and correct her reasoning on a changed case under the allowed reference. This is needed for Friday's report. | Two learner-hours for attempt, feedback use, correction and check; one 45-minute teacher session, including preparation and review. |
| B — adapt a data query | A query works on the practised structure. The remaining task is to adapt it to a changed structure and check the result with the permitted reference. No further topic reading is needed on the stipulated evidence. | Two learner-hours and one 45-minute teacher session for the remaining attempt, correction and check. |
| C — explore simulation | This is a proposed start, not an acquired contribution. One supported model and a contrast with the current analysis would inform whether a further simulation programme is worth constructing. That decision ends this exploration. | Two learner-hours and one 45-minute teacher session for the bounded exploration and its review. |

All three fit the six learner-hours but need 135 teacher-minutes; only 90 are available. Counting A's completed calculation and B's completed query as closed learning would conceal this competition. There are at least two comparable continuations that preserve Friday's requirement:

- **Continue A and B; defer C.** Four learner-hours and 90 teacher-minutes are allocated to the two remaining task contributions. Completion is intended, not guaranteed by those allowances.
- **Continue A and open C; pause B.** The same four learner-hours and 90 teacher-minutes supply A and the exploration. On the stipulated pause arrangement, preserving B's partial work takes another half-hour now and returning to it requires a further half-hour next month. Its remaining practice is still owed, and its later use must tolerate that delay.

The two continuations have different closure, option and transition consequences. HCD.2 returns those differences and a boundary of these two compatible active lines, not a universal maximum of two or a choice made for Lena. If the next project now requires simulation while B's later use is cancelled, opening C and retiring B can become preferable; unfinished status is not a reason to retain obsolete work.

Under the original work estimates, a confirmed third timely teacher session would make the three-line candidate feasible at six learner-hours and 135 teacher-minutes. This widens the available comparison without establishing that taking all three is preferable.

Suppose instead that A's next attempt reveals another correction requiring one learner-hour and a further 45-minute teacher session before Friday. A now consumes three learner-hours and both sessions. The previous two-line continuations no longer fit. With the same help, a candidate can keep only A active and pay B's half-hour pause cost: 3.5 learner-hours and 90 teacher-minutes. Retaining B or starting C as described requires additional suitable help or a changed arrangement. HCD.9's result changes the remaining work; HCD.14/.15 reopen the affected comparison.

### HCD.2:6 - Bias-Annotation

Lenses: **Gov**, **Arch**, **Onto/Epist**, **Prag**, **Did**. Scope: personal human-capability programme composition and comparison under qualified later-Work, participation, support, and evidence conditions.

| Recurring bias | Likely drift | Repair |
| --- | --- | --- |
| course-solution bias | The requested course or familiar programme is treated as the answer before later Work and baseline are recovered. | Begin from the holder, complete work tasks, current configuration, and supplied development stake. |
| detailed-candidate bias | The most documented candidate appears superior to sketches. | Compare one minimal closed-task fragment on the same positions before expanding the candidates. |
| topic-count bias | Coverage or PatternID count substitutes for contribution to later Work. | Trace every included element to task closure, a prerequisite, a support contribution, an evidence need, or a future option. |
| role-average bias | Audience or role assumptions become one person's current profile. | Require compatible same-holder evidence or issue the learning-product design return. |
| support invisibility | Teacher, assessor, specialist, AI, access, and preparation are assumed free and available. | Record access allocations, actual availability, peak load, and missing enablement separately. |
| assistance attribution | Helped output is treated as independent human capability or learning. | Preserve permitted, available, received, independent, changed-condition, and delayed evidence states. |
| sunk-curriculum bias | Existing content is retained because it was expensive to create. | Compare the finite contribution and displacement of retaining it under the current task and budget. |
| technique-brand bias | A pedagogy label is assumed to work across holders and tasks. | State its proposed mechanism, source limit, required observation, and serious alternative. |

### HCD.2:7 - Conformance Checklist

- [ ] One exact human holder is named for a personal comparison; an unknown audience receives a learning-product design return rather than an invented profile.
- [ ] The later-Work family, supplied development stake, protected outputs and errors, configuration, horizon, participation, evidence window, decision owner, and outside owners are explicit.
- [ ] The baseline contains only supported current human and external contributions under stated conditions.
- [ ] Every programme candidate closes or tests a recognizable complete-task combination rather than merely covering topics.
- [ ] Human recognition and performance, reference retrieval, controlled AI help and checking, specialist returns, and other provider contributions are allocated explicitly.
- [ ] True prerequisites are distinguished from supports and complements used during the same later Work.
- [ ] Preparation, representative attempts, feedback, correction, retries, changed-condition or delayed checks, and provider/access work are inside the candidate account.
- [ ] Candidates use the same decision-bearing output, error, burden, support, horizon, uncertainty, and future-option positions; unequal detail is reported as a gap.
- [ ] Learner, teacher, assessor, specialist, transition, tool, material, and displaced-work burdens are visible where they change the comparison.
- [ ] When another start competes with unfinished learning, the comparison recovers remaining work, compares closure with opening an option, and states which lines can remain active together, when another may start and what would change that boundary.
- [ ] Supported, independent, changed-condition, transfer, and retention claims remain distinct, and unobserved gains remain hypotheses.
- [ ] Any dominance wording is bounded to the candidates, coordinates, horizon, conditions, and evidence actually compared.
- [ ] The result contains a usable disposition and smallest reopen condition but no final choice, authorization, launch, provider-operation, or effectiveness claim.

### HCD.2:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Anti-pattern | Why it fails | Repair |
| --- | --- | --- |
| “Give everyone programme C” | Detail and a broad audience description do not establish personal fit. | Keep C as one design candidate; obtain same-holder inputs before personal comparison. |
| “This programme covers more topics” | Topic count says nothing about task closure, displacement, support, or evidence. | Compare contributions to complete later-Work results and protected errors. |
| “Scale 340 hours to 204” | Uniform scaling can remove preparation, attempts, feedback, or correction that makes the output plausible. | Name every removed or replaced hour and show how the required mechanisms and outputs remain available. |
| “Teacher hours make it feasible” | A time calculation does not establish competence, access, scheduling, or operation at peak load. | Obtain the HCD.7 support result or return the exact missing contribution to HCD.8 for obtain-or-build comparison and the preparation or operating test the selected route needs. |
| “AI support means the person knows it” | Assisted performance can differ from later unassisted performance. | Allocate the human checking contribution and preserve actual help in every observation. |
| “Every component is a prerequisite” | A printed sequence turns legitimate same-task references and specialists into unnecessary memorization or gates. | Separate before-practice prerequisites from simultaneous complements and supports. |
| “One feasible candidate dominates” | Missing rivals or evidence do not create a supported dominance relation. | Return the feasible description and the exact comparison gap. |
| “HCD.2 chooses and launches” | Comparison is collapsed with preference, authority, commitment, and execution. | Pass the comparison to the applicable decision Method and authorized owner. |
| “The course author is the learner” | Recipient and holder are silently merged. | Return a class-level design question now and reopen personal comparison when a named learner supplies compatible evidence. |

### HCD.2:9 - Consequences

The practitioner gains a comparison that connects development activities to complete later Work, exposes external support before commitment, and preserves uncertainty without becoming silent. A small comparable fragment can be enough to improve a decision, so the method does not require building several complete courses first.

The cost is explicit composition work. Human and provider time, access, transitions, retries, displaced practice, and later evidence can make an attractive programme infeasible. Some requests return to learning-product design, provider enablement, target-domain owners, or a separate target decision rather than yielding a personal recommendation.

### HCD.2:10 - Rationale

Development is configuration-relative. What one programme adds depends on what this person can already contribute, what support is actually available, which complete tasks matter, and which protected errors cannot be traded away. Starting from an empty curriculum exaggerates every addition; starting from a role average fabricates the holder.

Whole tasks reveal coordination and applicability, while claim-sized contribution allocation prevents the whole-task label from hiding references, AI, specialists, or prerequisites. Comparing finite changes keeps resources and displaced work visible. Separating comparison from choice protects preference, authority, commitment, launch, and evidence of effect as their own questions.

### HCD.2:11 - SoTA-Echoing

The working question is: **How should a practitioner compose and compare a development programme for one person's consequential later Work without reducing it to topics or promising an unobserved effect?**

The selected best-known line combines sufficiently whole complex-task practice with expertise-sensitive support, explicit correction and retesting where those mechanisms fit, and configuration-relative finite comparison. The maintained [4C/ID model](https://www.4cid.org/about/) and its [fourth-edition presentation](https://www.4cid.org/readings/books/) supply the serious complex-task design candidate: whole learning tasks, support for non-routine reasoning, timely procedural information, and additional practice for recurrent parts. Paas and van Merriënboer's 2020 review ([`COG-05`](https://doi.org/10.1177/0963721420922183)) supports changing guidance with prior knowledge and task complexity. Winget and Persky's 2022 review ([`COG-06`](https://doi.org/10.5688/ajpe8906)) supplies the bounded formative-assessment, corrective-activity, retest, and threshold arrangement. HCD.2 adapts these contributions into §§4.2–4.3; none establishes later professional performance or the effect of a local programme.

The serious ordinary alternative is a syllabus-first or branded-programme comparison: list content and hours, match them to a role profile, then prefer the most complete or familiar package. It is cheaper to describe, but it hides complete-task closure, same-holder starting evidence, contribution allocations, provider dependence, displaced work, and unequal detail. HCD.2 rejects topic count and programme labels as the comparison basis, while retaining a syllabus as one carrier of a candidate once its contribution is made explicit.

`C.11.CRC` supplies the internal finite-comparison grammar used in §4.4. The HCD evidence chain keeps intended instruction, supported attempts, independent performance, transfer, and retention in their direct pattern owners; HCD.2 carries only the expectations and evidence needs used by the comparison. Bastani and colleagues' 2025 school-mathematics trial ([`AI-04`](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2422633122)) is counterexample evidence that improved AI-assisted practice can fail to improve later unassisted performance; its population and task do not supply an adult workplace effect size or a universal AI prohibition. These limits produce the separate evidence states in §§4.3–4.6 rather than a promised causal programme effect.

This comparison adds design and evidence work, but it is non-dominated for the stated question because it preserves complete-task usefulness, personal fit, support dependence, finite burden, and uncertainty that the cheaper syllabus-first alternative loses. Reopen the selected line if a stronger source changes the complex-task, support, correction, AI-dependence, or transfer boundary, or if representative use shows that the same decision values can be preserved with materially less effort.

### HCD.2:12 - Relations

- **`HCD.1`:** can supply the compatible human capability-demand account and later-Work boundary; programme composition does not alter that demand.
- **`HCD.3`:** can supply a qualified human target or non-training return when rival causes change the programme; diagnosis is not mandatory otherwise.
- **`HCD.4`:** can supply the current/target claim comparison, protected strengths, priorities, and trade-offs; a profile does not generate programme alternatives.
- **`HCD.5`:** selects human-development Methods for the target contribution and evidence limits exposed by a candidate.
- **`HCD.6`:** designs representative practice tasks, permitted help, variations, and result criteria needed by the selected Method.
- **`HCD.7`:** establishes which provider, source, tool, AI, access, and human-check contributions are actually available.
- **`HCD.8`:** compares obtaining or building an exact unavailable contribution and establishes the preparation or operating test the selected route needs; already established usable support can be arranged directly through HCD.7.
- **`HCD.9` and `HCD.10`:** carry out focused practice and change its variation, spacing, interleaving, challenge, or help while preserving attempt history.
- **`HCD.11`–`HCD.13`:** provide compatible observed performance, transfer, retention, and support-dependence evidence; the programme description does not manufacture those observations.
- **`HCD.14` and `HCD.15`:** revise affected programme assumptions and parts, or reopen development when later Work or support changes; changes in remaining work or available help can revise the boundary on concurrent learning.
- **`C.11.CRC`:** supplies the finite configuration-relative comparison claim. **`C.11`** separately supplies a bounded choice when its preference, belief, outcome, probe, and authority inputs exist.
- **PSD and other advice Methods:** may recommend a programme to a named recipient from qualified inputs; advice does not compose the missing programme or make the choice for its owner.
- **HCD.28:** constructs and compares a whole learning product for a future audience, using HCD.5–8 and other applicable contributions. HCD.2 returns the unknown-audience question there and consumes suitable variants only with compatible personal evidence.
- **Learning-product and target-domain practices:** supply applicable instructional/carrier construction and professional task correctness. HCD.28 coordinates the needed product contributions; HCD.2 returns an exact missing domain question without inventing its answer.
- **Provider, clinical, safety, legal, employment, specialist, organization, and release owners:** retain their direct competence, participation, authority, and consequence decisions.

### HCD.2:End

## HCD.5 - Select Human Capability-Development Methods

> **Type:** Human Capability Development practitioner method-selection pattern
> **Status:** Stable

### HCD.5:0 - Use This When

Use this pattern to select how to develop a particular contribution. For a known person, begin with a qualified target and an initial or recent attempt. For a future audience, begin with the intended contribution and the entry conditions that would call for different teaching or practice. Return conditional design choices until evidence about a particular learner supports applying one of them.

The first useful result is a **Method-selection account**: a justified set of capability-development Methods, the target contribution and proposed mechanism for each, their task and learner fit, required support, evidence limits, burden and risk, surviving alternatives, and the observation that would change the selection. The result can contain one Method or a small coordinated set. A future-audience result states the entry evidence on which each choice depends. Selection does not establish target engagement, learning, transfer, or effectiveness.

The practical gain is discrimination. A person who calculates correctly but accepts an unsupported cause receives a different development proposal from someone who cannot perform the calculation, cannot recognize when the Method applies, or lacks the data and permission to act. An external constraint is returned to its owner instead of being disguised as a need for more training.

Do not use HCD.5 to diagnose a disorder or human limitation, design the full practice task, assign a provider, launch an intervention, or infer development from participation. Use HCD.3 when rival causes still change the human target. Use HCD.6 to turn a selected Method into representative tasks, HCD.7–HCD.8 for support and provider arrangements, and HCD.9–HCD.14 for enactment and evidence.

#### HCD.5:0.1 - Working Terms

| Name in this pattern | What it denotes |
| --- | --- |
| development target | The smallest supported change in the person's contribution that the proposed development should address under the named conditions. A score, trait label, activity, or programme topic is not the target by itself. |
| starting attempt | A condition-qualified observation of the person's relevant action before the selected development. Record the task, help received, work product, result, and important errors rather than only a score. |
| conditional design hypothesis | A proposed Method choice for a future learner whose entry evidence would meet stated conditions. It identifies the required evidence without asserting that any person already meets those conditions. |
| capability-development Method | A repeatable way of arranging human action, task, information, feedback, support, and correction to pursue a named development target. Its description guides action; it does not establish that the Method was enacted or effective. |
| proposed mechanism | The instructional reason the Method is expected to change the target, with the learner action and conditions that could make it useful. This can be a revisable design hypothesis; it need not assert a known neural mechanism or a demonstrated causal effect. |
| observed target change | A difference in the selected target between observations under stated conditions. It can inform the next development decision before its cause is established. |
| target engagement | A change in the selected target attributable to an intervention. Evidence must concern that target and justify the attribution; a theory label or assigned activity does neither. |
| Method set | One Method or a small combination whose members make distinct necessary contributions to the same bounded target or task. A catalogue of plausible techniques is not a selected set. |
| surviving alternative | A serious alternative that remains compatible with the current evidence and would change the development action or evidence plan. |
| non-training return | A return naming the external constraint, owner, blocked HCD decision, safe interim boundary, and retry condition when a human-development Method is not yet the supported next move. |

The target, selected Method, Method description, provider, enacted development Work, observed target change, and later capability claim remain different objects. HCD.5 selects the Method and records the description and conditions needed by the next design use; later evidence determines what was enacted and what changed.

### HCD.5:1 - Problem Frame

The same poor result can arise from different action failures. A person may lack a usable explanation, make a recurrent calculation error, fail to distinguish situations that call for different Methods, or combine individually correct steps badly in a whole task. The same visible failure may instead come from missing data, inaccessible sources, absent permission, an unsuitable tool, an unavailable specialist, or an unsafe workload.

Development Methods act differently. A worked example can expose reasoning that unsupported problem solving hides, but unchanged guidance can obstruct an experienced learner. Part practice can stabilize a recurrent operation, but it cannot teach when to use it. Whole tasks can expose coordination, but they can overload a novice when a true prerequisite is missing. Feedback can change the next attempt only when its information identifies an actionable difference.

Method selection connects a qualified target and starting attempt—or explicitly assumed entry conditions for a future audience—to a plausible change mechanism, while preserving the task, learner, support, evidence, burden, and risk conditions under which that mechanism might help.

### HCD.5:2 - Problem

The common shortcut is treatment by label: “deliberate practice,” “coaching,” “mastery,” “retrieval,” “interleaving,” “motivation,” or “AI tutor” is prescribed because the term sounds relevant. The label hides what the person must do differently and which observation would show that the proposed target changed.

Another shortcut chooses the activity that is easiest to provide. A lecture substitutes for missing project access, repeated calculation substitutes for causal discrimination, or a score substitutes for feedback. The intervention can be delivered successfully while the limiting contribution remains untouched.

The opposite failure is an exhaustive menu with no selection. The practitioner needs a small justified Method set, one serious alternative, and a precise return when the next step is not human development.

### HCD.5:3 - Forces

- A familiar technique is easy to commission, while its mechanism may not match the observed action or later-Work target.
- Whole-task practice preserves coordination, while a true prerequisite or recurrent suboperation may need focused preparation.
- Guidance can help a novice begin, while the same guidance can become redundant or answer-bearing as knowledge grows.
- Repetition supplies more attempts, while repeated practice history alone does not establish causality or a universal hours threshold.
- Feedback is widely available, while its information content, timing, receiver, and opportunity for correction determine what it can change.
- A self-regulation plan can support an already endorsed goal, while goal enactment is not the same as capability or transfer.
- Supported performance can make practice possible, while it can hide the human contribution the target requires.
- A small source effect can justify a candidate mechanism, while population, task, measure, horizon, and provider differences limit transfer to this person.
- Human development can be useful, while access, authority, environment, provider, safety, clinical, or target-domain problems may own the next action.

### HCD.5:4 - Solution

Recover the target action and its observed or proposed entry conditions, compare a small set of Methods that propose materially different change mechanisms, and select only the Method or combination whose task fit, learner fit, support, burden, risk, and evidence plan remain credible. Return external constraints before prescribing development.

Use observations of the target to decide whether to continue or change practice. Report the conditions and what changed; a before/after difference alone does not identify the intervention's effect. Obtain additional causal evidence only when the receiving decision needs that stronger claim and the inquiry is feasible and worth its cost. If the target observation is unavailable, leave change unknown rather than treating it as a demonstrated lack of improvement.

#### HCD.5:4.1 - Bind the Selection Use

First distinguish selection for a known person from design for a future audience. Name:

1. the person and participation basis, or the future audience and its assumptions; identify the receiving decision and decision owner in either case;
2. the later-Work contribution, configuration, horizon, protected result and critical-error conditions;
3. the qualified target for that person and any still-plausible rival explanation, or the target contribution and proposed entry conditions for each design branch;
4. the person's starting attempt, including task, permitted and received help, work product, result, errors, uncertainty and evidence window. For future design, state instead the entry task or existing evidence that would distinguish the branches, the allowed help and the response that would select or reopen each choice;
5. current strengths, prior relevant practice, available time, access, tools, AI posture, provider contribution, environment, privacy, safety, and other protected conditions; and
6. the observation that the receiving decision would use after the Method is applied.

For future design, keep unknown learner, support and resource values as assumptions with a return condition. Apply a personal choice only when the person's entry evidence supports it. If rival explanations then change the human target or next action, return to HCD.3. If a target-domain way or judgement required for the next action is unavailable, or access, permission, a tool, specialist result or safe participation condition is missing, return that specific need to its owner. A qualified demonstration, family of exemplars or practitioner judgement can supply a usable subject basis before it is fully verbalized; §4.2.1 develops that branch. Do not make an actually missing contribution into a motivation, practice or knowledge deficit.

#### HCD.5:4.2 - Generate a Small Candidate Set by Mechanism

Use the observed action difference, or the stated difference between possible entry conditions, to generate serious candidates. The following cues are questions, not an exhaustive intervention classification:

| Observed difference | Candidate Method question | Boundary to preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the person lacks a usable representation or cannot follow expert reasoning | Would an explanation, demonstration, integrated worked example, or prompted self-explanation expose the decision-bearing relation? | Guidance should fit prior knowledge and later be reduced or changed; understanding the example is not independent performance. |
| the person cannot yet notice the difference named by an instruction | Would HCD.6.1 make that difference discernible through an accessible contrast and a response that uses it? | The encounter must be feasible from the learner's existing capabilities; noticing the difference and performing the target action remain separate. |
| the person performs an operation when named but does not recognize when it applies | Would discrimination practice across contrasting situations improve recognition and Method selection? | Repeating execution with the Method name supplied cannot test this target. |
| a recurrent component is slow or error-prone and constrains the whole task | Would focused part practice with immediate correction stabilize that component? | The component must contribute to the later task; part success does not establish whole-task coordination. |
| separate contributions are adequate but their coordination fails | Would sufficiently whole-task practice with bounded support expose the interfaces and stopping conditions? | A true prerequisite may still need preparation; task realism does not excuse unsafe or uninterpretable complexity. |
| the next attempt repeats a known, actionable difference | What information-specific feedback, corrective activity, and retest would let the person change that action? | Praise, a score, or another attempt is not enough when it does not identify the difference to change. |
| the person has an endorsed goal and feasible action but misses a stable cue | Would a bounded if–then plan or environmental cue support enactment? | Goal attainment is not capability, and a plan cannot repair an unavailable or unsafe action. |
| competent participation in complex Work is needed | Would demonstration, coaching, guided participation, or supervised workplace practice provide the missing contribution? | The provider, task, access, supervision, and consequence boundary must be real; the label “apprenticeship” establishes none of them. |
| the observed limit disappears when data, permission, workload, tool, or support is restored | Is the supported next move an access or arrangement change rather than a development Method? | Return the condition to HCD.7, HCD.8, or its direct owner and preserve any remaining human target separately. |

Spacing, retrieval, interleaving, cue focus, support fading, and other practice features may refine a candidate when their mechanism matches the target. Their names do not select the Method. HCD.10 chooses the condition-sensitive practice change after the governing Method and observations are present.

If a local proficiency model is being used, connect the candidate mechanism to its proposed transition rather than selecting a Method for a level name. Recover the starting response, the intended difference and the condition that distinguishes them from HCD.4:4.2.1–4.2.2. For N24 (HCD.6:5.6), correct calculation with a supplied unit rules against arithmetic repetition as the present target. Contrast and supported whole performance are serious alternatives for making unit selection available. If later evidence separates cue-dependent selection from cue-resistant selection, reconsider that mechanism and its task; the model's new wording alone is no reason to repeat an unchanged Method. Pass the selected connection and its uncertainty to HCD.6.


##### HCD.5:4.2.1 - Compose learning from the contribution, not an explicit–implicit ratio

Use this branch when a rule lesson, repeated imitation or unstructured participation leaves a person unable to use what they encounter. The aim is a feasible combination in which each activity supplies something the next contribution needs. The combination can begin with an explanation, a demonstration, an existing successful performance or participation in work; the entry evidence decides.

**Recover the practice and the kind of judgement.** Identify the receiving activity and an adequate performance, together with a nearby case that calls for a different response. Correctness can be specified by a rule, but it can also be made accessible through recordings, competent demonstrations, accepted work products, partner responses or qualified practitioner judgement. Establish the conditions in which those comparisons have standing. Where competent practitioners differ, preserve the different conventions or purposes and teach a useful choice between them. If the required distinction remains unsupported, narrow that target or obtain subject help. Incomplete verbalization alone does not make a demonstrated practice unavailable.

Distinguish a learner's ability to explain a regularity from their ability to notice, anticipate or enact it. Likewise distinguish a teaching activity from a claim about the learner's psychological mechanism. Learning from examples can include deliberate comparison; a fluent response can have a history of explicit instruction. Failure to verbalize an acquired distinction does not establish that its acquisition was unconscious. Neural-network learning can suggest questions about exposure, variation or prediction, but that analogy supplies no evidence of the human mechanism.

**Find the missing contribution in an attainable whole use.** Use an existing work sample or a small supported encounter, rather than demand an unaided test from someone who cannot yet enter the task. Ask what the person can already supply and what the current help supplies. Then choose the contribution that will change the next attempt:

| Present need | Construct the learning opportunity | Use its result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Understand why a choice or boundary matters | Give a short explanation connected to contrasting cases; let the learner predict or choose in another case. | Use the relation to guide selection, diagnose an exception or ask a better question. A repeated definition is insufficient when action is the target. |
| Notice or anticipate a pattern before a full account is available | Supply accessible, meaningful examples and contrasts across the relevant family; let the learner discriminate, predict, complete or respond. | Use the response to locate a confusion and refine examples or help through HCD.6.1. Do not require an invented rule for every successful discrimination. |
| Make an available operation more fluent or stable | Arrange manageable repetitions with information about the result and a correction the learner can use. | Reduce demands on the encompassing activity, then return the operation to it. Mere familiarity with a model may leave production unchanged. |
| Coordinate contributions that work separately | Keep the consequential coupling in a reduced-demand whole task; support other contributions and practise the missing relation. | Restore tempo, complexity, partners or conditions as the intended use requires. Part success alone cannot decide that return. |
| Adapt a familiar response | Contrast conditions in which it works with conditions requiring a change; vary the deciding relation while preserving usable references. | Let the person select, modify, pause or seek help in a new relevant case. Include a valid familiar case so that blanket refusal is not rewarded. |
| Participate competently in changing work or culture | Give a useful, attainable contribution with access to competent participants, feedback and another occasion to contribute. | Increase or change participation from what the person can supply and what the practice needs. Attendance alone supplies neither the opportunity nor the learning. |

**Choose what to explain and when to bring it into attention.** Explain a relation when it can make the next action intelligible, expose a misconception, protect a consequential boundary or help transfer. Demonstrate or contrast what a description leaves imperceptible. During a difficult whole performance, one usable cue may serve better than simultaneous monitoring of every component. Inspect a detail between attempts, practise it under manageable conditions, then let the learner return attention to the purpose, partner or result of the whole. If conscious monitoring already helps, keep it. If it disrupts an otherwise available coordination, compare a different cue or a separate preparation episode. The appropriate focus is a subject- and learner-dependent design choice.

**Build a distribution of encounters, not only a rule and one exception.** Frequent forms can deserve repeated use; rare but consequential exceptions can deserve deliberate contrasts or an available reference. Include meaningful variation in speakers, situations, materials or partners where later work will require it. A teaching set may intentionally overrepresent a difficult exception. Tell the learner enough about that choice to avoid mistaking exercise frequency for prevalence in the practice. There is no universal proportion of rule-governed and example-based learning, including a 70/30 split. Allocations of time should follow the missing contribution, encounter opportunities, consequence and response.

**Distinguish learning a convention, switching conventions and changing one.** For reproduction, provide examples and feedback from the practice the learner wants to join. For switching, contrast situations with different purposes or expectations and practise recognizing which convention is in use. For deliberate innovation, let the learner vary a consequential relation while retaining a chosen contribution, then examine the variant with competent participants in its receiving use. A successful experiment can support keeping that variant locally; wider adoption and a changed cultural norm are further results. Music and dance practice development returns those questions to MDPE.21/.17 and Application:5. Learning to take part in that work remains an HCD question.

**Join activities through actual use.** An explanation can supply a distinction for comparing examples. A contrast can make an instruction perceptible. Repetition can make a response available quickly enough to coordinate with another action. Participation can expose the context or exception that changes the next explanation. State which of these joins is needed here and give the learner the corresponding action. Do not add all activities to every lesson or presume a one-way progression from theory to practice.

Choose the next observation from the pending decision. If learners can recognize the pattern but cannot enact it, change practice rather than add more recognition questions. If they perform only with a model, decide whether that support belongs to later work or whether another occasion should expose selection without it. If their response fits one register or partner convention, extend the experience only when another use is needed. Stop the added development when the supported arrangement serves the present purpose.

This construction is a reasoned teaching hypothesis. Use established subject knowledge, available observations and current learning research to choose a worthwhile action; an unattainable controlled experiment is not a prerequisite for trying a proportionate arrangement. Retain what is uncertain when it changes use. Commission a further comparison when its attainable answer can change the teaching choice or justify a stronger claim enough to warrant its cost. C.11.DUA develops that comparison; it neither converts a plausible mechanism into a demonstrated effect nor requires a study merely to finish this design.

#### HCD.5:4.3 - Compare Method Fit and Evidence

For each serious candidate, record:

| Selection position | Required content |
| --- | --- |
| target contribution | The exact human action or judgement intended to change and its role in later Work. |
| proposed mechanism | How the Method is expected to change that target, what source or prior observation supports the expectation, and which rival explanation remains live. |
| task and learner fit | Starting performance, prior knowledge, task complexity, similarity, support dependence, and the reason this Method fits better than the serious alternative. |
| enacted form | The minimally sufficient explanation, demonstration, practice, feedback, correction, plan, coaching, or support change; identify a qualified professional description when local design would be unsafe or under-specified. |
| provider and access need | Competence, time, data, tools, AI, environment, supervision, permission, privacy, and peak-load conditions required for the Method. |
| burden and risk | Learner and provider effort, displaced Work, error exposure, overload, autonomy, fatigue, clinical or safety risk, and the cost of another attempt or probe. |
| evidence plan | Use existing observations when sufficient. Select further observation only for a question that can change the choice or qualify a needed claim; retain the relevant help, conditions and inference limits. A design hypothesis can guide an attainable next action without a separate causal study. |
| alternatives and stop | Surviving alternative, rejected candidate with reason, condition for stopping or returning, and smallest change that reopens selection. |

Compare candidates at comparable enactment effort. A richly specified Method does not defeat an unnamed alternative; make only the smallest alternative description needed to expose a decision-bearing difference. Preserve source limits instead of transporting one average effect, hours threshold, cue, sequence, or professional arrangement to a different task and population.

#### HCD.5:4.4 - Select a Coherent Method Set

Select the smallest set whose members make distinct contributions to the target. For a combination, state:

1. which target or task difference each member addresses;
2. whether it prepares a prerequisite, enables the first attempt, supplies feedback, supports correction, or tests changed performance;
3. which order is required by dependence and which order is merely convenient;
4. which help is allowed during each observation and what the person must do without an answer-bearing cue; and
5. when the set stops, changes, or returns because comparable observations show insufficient target change, another limitation appears, or a provider condition fails.

Do not accumulate techniques as insurance. If two candidates propose the same contribution at higher burden, retain the lower-burden adequate candidate unless a material evidence, safety, participation, or future-use value justifies the difference. If methods address different supported targets, keep those targets and evidence plans distinct even when one programme coordinates their enactment.

#### HCD.5:4.5 - Record the Method-Selection Account

| Result position | Required content |
| --- | --- |
| selection boundary | Person and participation basis, or future audience assumptions; later-Work contribution, configuration, horizon, evidence window, receiving decision, decision owner and outside owners. Mark which conditions are observed and which are proposed. |
| target and start | For personal selection: qualified target and starting attempt with its conditions, strengths, errors, help, uncertainty and still-plausible rivals. For future design: target contribution, assumed starting conditions and the entry evidence that would select or reopen each branch. |
| selected Method set | Each Method's action, proposed mechanism, intended target contribution, enacted form, required support, and stop condition. |
| comparison | Serious alternatives, comparable effort, task and learner fit, evidence, burden, risk, and reason for selection or rejection. |
| evidence plan | Existing basis and any worthwhile next observation; help and changed conditions that affect interpretation; stronger later-Work evidence only for a needed stronger claim; limits that change use. |
| disposition | `selected Method set`, `conditional design hypothesis for stated entry evidence`, `non-training return`, or `Method description or provider result blocked`. |
| continuation | The practice-task design, provider/access result, first enacted attempt, missing professional description, outside-owner question, or smallest condition that reopens selection. |

For a future audience, return only a conditional design hypothesis tied to the stated entry evidence and planned diagnostic branches. Do not turn an audience description into an individual prescription. When a competent professional Method or provider result is required and unavailable, name that result rather than writing a generic local substitute.

#### HCD.5:4.6 - Recognition and Assurance

**Recognition.** Use HCD.5 when the question is “What kind of development activity could change this person's specific action?” and a worked example, whole task, focused component practice, feedback loop, coaching arrangement, self-regulation aid, or support change would lead to different next Work. For a future audience, ask the same question conditionally for each proposed entry branch.

**Assurance.** Stronger reliance needs a qualified target, condition-compatible starting evidence, a task- and learner-matched mechanism claim, source limits, credible provider and access conditions, material burden and risk, and an observation that can detect target change without conflating helped performance with learning. Attribution of that change to the intervention requires a further basis; it is not implied by this observation. Clinical, safety, employment, legal, provider-competence, and target-domain correctness decisions require their direct owners.

#### HCD.5:4.7 - What Changes in Practice

A practitioner stops asking, “Which learning technique should we use?” and asks, “Which exact action must change, what Method could change it under these conditions, what serious alternative remains, and what observation would show that the target—not merely the activity or score—changed?” When the answer is access, permission, data, workload, or specialist input, the work leaves Method selection with a named return.

### HCD.5:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### HCD.5:5.1 - Correct Calculation, Unsupported Cause

In a constructed pump case, flow remains 100 m³/h while measured power rises from 20 to 22.4 kW, so the calculated energy per unit volume rises by 12%. The person computes the ratio correctly but concludes that the controller change caused the increase. Current facts leave at least resistance, regulation efficiency, and measurement error as live explanations.

The target is not unit conversion or arithmetic. It is proposing competing explanations, stating a discriminating observation, and keeping the conclusion conditional. A selected Method set uses one worked explanation that makes the rival predictions visible, a coached discrimination attempt, and a later changed case in which the person must choose the next observation without the Method or answer supplied. Focused unit practice remains a surviving candidate only if a separate starting observation shows a unit error. Generic repetition of the original calculation is rejected because it does not address the target.

The selection account records the proposed reasoning mechanism, teacher feedback needed, safe stipulated data, changed-condition observation, and the limit that this exercise does not establish engineering capability or the causal effect of the Method.

#### HCD.5:5.2 - Execution with a Cue, Failure to Select

A person can apply a finite comparison correctly whenever `C.11.CRC` is named, yet chooses a local score when a new situation requires comparing complete configurations. More worked examples with the PatternID printed beside the task would rehearse execution while preserving the selection failure.

HCD.5 selects discrimination practice across cases in which a finite comparison, a sensitivity result, or a source check is appropriate. Early feedback names the decision-bearing cue; later tasks remove the answer-bearing Method label and change the configuration or horizon. The intended observation is correct recognition and selection before execution on the changed case. It can support this performance claim without yet establishing whether the practice caused the change. HCD.6 supplies the actual representative task set; HCD.9 records what happened in each attempt.

#### HCD.5:5.3 - Missing Project Access Is Not a Practice Dose

A participant can explain the target Method on a supplied case but cannot apply it in their work because the project data and permission for a small safe trial are absent. The missing access changes the next action before any learning-technique comparison. HCD.5 returns the exact data, permission, owner, blocked practice decision, and retry condition to HCD.7 or the direct project owner. It preserves any supported human target but does not prescribe a longer course or call non-participation low motivation.

#### HCD.5:5.4 - Future Audience Design Hypothesis

A learning-product author expects entrants to differ in unit work, causal discrimination, and Method recognition. HCD.5 may propose conditional branches: focused component preparation for an observed unit error, worked explanation and coached discrimination for an unsupported cause, and Method-selection practice for cue dependence. The author still needs entry tasks that distinguish those conditions. The branch is not a frequency claim about engineers or a prescription for any person not yet observed.

### HCD.5:6 - Bias-Annotation

Lenses: **Gov**, **Arch**, **Onto/Epist**, **Prag**, **Did**. Scope: selecting capability-development Methods from a person's qualified target and starting evidence, or proposing conditional choices for a future audience.

| Recurring bias | Likely drift | Repair |
| --- | --- | --- |
| technique allegiance | One school or branded intervention becomes the default. | Compare proposed mechanisms and a serious alternative against the exact target and starting attempt. |
| activity bias | Attendance, repetition, coaching time, or content exposure substitutes for change in the target. | Name the observation of target change and distinguish it from an intervention-effect claim. |
| deficit bias | A tool, access, authority, workload, provider, or specialist failure becomes a human limitation. | Issue a non-training return while preserving any separately supported target. |
| score bias | A scalar selects an intervention without the underlying action or error. | Recover the task, work product, help, error pattern, and inference limit. |
| novice-default bias | Guidance is kept constant despite changing prior knowledge. | State the learner-fit condition and the rule for reducing, changing, or removing support. |
| dose bias | More hours or repetitions are presumed causal. | Specify the Method contribution and observation; keep practice history as evidence rather than mechanism proof. |
| feedback optimism | Any response from a teacher or tool is called useful feedback. | State the information that identifies the action to change and the opportunity for correction. |
| motivation rhetoric | A theory label explains non-enactment without target or context evidence. | Compare cue, feasibility, support, environment, and the observed target before selecting a self-regulation Method. |

### HCD.5:7 - Conformance Checklist

- [ ] The selection concerns either a known person with a qualified target or a future audience with explicit entry assumptions; the intended contribution, horizon, receiving decision and decision owner are recoverable.
- [ ] A personal selection uses a starting attempt with its conditions, help, work product, result, errors, strengths and uncertainty. A future-audience proposal identifies the entry evidence needed to distinguish its conditional branches without asserting that a learner has supplied it.
- [ ] External access, Method, tool, authority, provider, specialist, clinical, safety, or environment constraints are returned to their direct owners rather than renamed as training needs.
- [ ] Every serious candidate states a proposed mechanism, target contribution, task and learner fit, minimally sufficient enacted form, required support, burden, risk, and evidence plan.
- [ ] The comparison includes one serious alternative at comparable enactment effort and preserves source population, task, measure, horizon, support, and causal limits.
- [ ] Whole-task, part-practice, explanation, feedback, coaching, planning, and support candidates are selected by their contribution, not by label.
- [ ] A selected combination assigns one distinct necessary contribution to each member and states required versus convenient order.
- [ ] Intended help, permitted help, actual availability, received help, and independent action remain distinct.
- [ ] Observed target change is distinguished from attendance, satisfaction and the intervention's effect. Assistance conditions limit the performance claim; later capability, transfer and retention need their own grounds.
- [ ] The result records surviving alternatives, rejected candidates with reasons, stop conditions, and the smallest change that reopens selection.
- [ ] A future-audience result is conditional on stated entry evidence and does not prescribe for an unobserved person.
- [ ] HCD.5 selects no provider, full task set, programme choice, intervention launch, clinical action, employment action, or effectiveness conclusion.

### HCD.5:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Anti-pattern | Why it fails | Repair |
| --- | --- | --- |
| “Use deliberate practice” | The label omits the target, task, feedback, refinement, provider, and evidence limits; accumulated practice is not a universal cause. | Specify the proposed mechanism and enacted form for this target, or choose another Method. |
| “They need more examples” | Examples may improve representation or preserve cue dependence; the action difference is unknown. | Compare worked explanation, discrimination practice, and independent selection against the observed error. |
| “The score is low, so reteach” | A score can mix arithmetic, recognition, support, access, and measurement error. | Recover the claim-sized starting attempt and live rivals first. |
| “Whole tasks are always best” | Missing prerequisites, overload, or safety conditions can make a whole task unusable. | Prepare the true prerequisite and retain sufficiently whole practice for the contributions that must combine. |
| “Remove all help” | Abrupt withdrawal can test the wrong thing or make practice unsafe. | Select help and its change by target, current knowledge, task, and intended observation. |
| “Feedback works” | A score, praise, or generic comment may not identify the next action. | Specify information content, receiver, correction opportunity, and retest. |
| “Write an if–then plan for any gap” | A plan cannot create capability, access, authority, or an unendorsed goal. | Use planning only for a supported enactment target with detectable cue and feasible response. |
| “The missing project proves low motivation” | No human inference follows from unavailable data or permission. | Return the access condition and retry predicate to its owner. |
| “Select every plausible technique” | The list hides contribution, sequence, burden, and stop conditions. | Keep the smallest coherent Method set and one serious surviving alternative. |

### HCD.5:9 - Consequences

The practitioner gains a reasoned bridge from a qualified target to a practice design and evidence plan. Different error patterns receive different candidate mechanisms, and a provider or access failure can stop unhelpful development before time is committed.

The cost is more precise starting evidence and explicit comparison. A selected Method may require a competent provider, safe task, additional observation, or professional description that is not yet available. Some familiar interventions will remain only conditional hypotheses, and observed failure to change the target can warrant reselection.

### HCD.5:10 - Rationale

A development activity is useful only through the contribution it changes for the receiving later-Work use. Technique names and average effects compress away the holder, task, starting action, support, and evidence boundary that determine local fit.

Mechanism comparison keeps the proposal generative without claiming causality in advance. The observation of target change makes failure informative: it can challenge the selected Method before a poor later result is blamed on the person. A small Method set preserves complementarity while preventing a catalogue from masquerading as a choice.

### HCD.5:11 - SoTA-Echoing

The working question is: **How should a practitioner select a human-development Method that fits one qualified target and starting attempt rather than merely choosing a familiar intervention label?**

The selected best-known line is target-, task-, learner-, and evidence-sensitive Method selection. Paas and van Merriënboer's 2020 review ([`COG-05`](https://doi.org/10.1177/0963721420922183)) supports integrated information and worked examples for avoidable novice load while requiring guidance to change with prior knowledge. Wisniewski, Zierer, and Hattie's 2020 meta-analysis ([`MOT-05`](https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2019.03087)) shows why feedback must be selected by information content, task, receiver, and opportunity to use it rather than by the claim that “feedback works.” Sheeran and colleagues' 2020 meta-analysis ([`MOT-01`](https://doi.org/10.1037/ccp0000501)) distinguishes an intervention's effect on its proposed target from that target's contribution to the later outcome. Its health-behaviour population and small average effect do not establish professional capability transfer. HCD uses this distinction to limit causal claims while allowing local decisions based on condition-qualified observations.

The serious ordinary alternative is intervention by family label: prescribe deliberate practice, mastery, coaching, motivation work, retrieval, interleaving, or AI tutoring from a broad diagnosis or a low score. It is cheaper to commission, but it cannot explain why the selected activity should change this action rather than a rival limitation. HCD.5 adapts the source line into the bound selection positions in §§4.1–4.5 and rejects a universal technique or dose.

Macnamara, Hambrick, and Oswald's 2014 meta-analysis ([`BEH-02`](https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797614535810)) is limit evidence: observed deliberate-practice histories account for different and incomplete shares of performance variance and do not establish a universal hours threshold or causal intervention. Sheeran and colleagues' 2024 planning synthesis ([`MOT-03`](https://doi.org/10.1080/10463283.2024.2334563)) supplies a bounded if–then planning candidate only when a goal is endorsed, a cue is detectable, and an action is feasible. Carpenter, Pan, and Butler's 2022 review ([`COG-01`](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44159-022-00089-1)) supports spacing and retrieval as candidates for durable access under source-specific conditions, not as a complete curriculum or default Method for every target.

The selected line costs more than matching labels to a catalogue, but it preserves target fit, external returns, provider needs, risks, and an observation capable of changing the selection. Reopen it when stronger source evidence changes a relied-on mechanism or limit, when target observations contradict the expected change, when the task or learner conditions change, or when a lower-effort selection practice preserves the same decision-bearing values.

Ren, Wang and Conway's [2024 meta-analysis](https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000897) reports that explicit instruction can improve statistical-learning task performance; it does not support an opposition between explaining and learning regularities from experience, or a universal advantage from increasingly detailed instruction. Section 4.2.1 uses that result to keep explanation and exposure available in one design. Its method composition is an authored construction, informed also by HCD.6's whole-task and HCD.6.1's perceptual-learning contributions; the complete arrangement has not been tested by those source studies.

### HCD.5:12 - Relations

- **`HCD.1`:** can supply the later-Work demand and protected contribution boundary.
- **`HCD.2`:** can expose programme components that need Method selection; HCD.5 does not choose the programme.
- **`HCD.3`:** supplies a qualified human target or non-training return when rival causes matter.
- **`HCD.4`:** can supply current strengths, priority characteristics, trade-offs, and condition-qualified profile evidence.
- **`HCD.6`:** turns the selected Method into representative tasks, permitted help, variations, and result criteria.
- **`HCD.7`:** establishes whether the required people, sources, tools, AI, access, environment, and checking contributions are available.
- **`HCD.8`:** builds a missing development arrangement only after the required provider or environment result is explicit.
- **`HCD.9` and `HCD.10`:** enact the selected focused practice and adjust its variation, spacing, interleaving, progression, or help from observed attempts.
- **`HCD.11`–`HCD.13`:** supply stronger same-holder performance, transfer, retention, and support-dependence evidence; HCD.5's mechanism claim does not substitute for those results.
- **`HCD.14`:** may revise the selected Method when compatible evidence changes the target, mechanism, fit, support, or result expectation.
- **Target-domain, clinical, safety, legal, employment, privacy, organization, provider, and specialist practices:** retain correctness, risk, participation, authority, and competence decisions.
- **Explanation Design:** when the selected activity needs an explanation, [EXD.1](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/EXPLANATION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#exd1---establish-and-revise-what-a-recipient-needs-explained) establishes the question, [EXD.2](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/EXPLANATION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#exd2---build-and-bound-an-explanatory-example) constructs an example that exposes the relevant relation and its limits, and [EXD.5](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/EXPLANATION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#exd5---guide-a-recipients-own-explanation) guides the learner's own explanation and correction. Use the needed contribution within HCD.6 task design or HCD.9 practice; HCD.10–HCD.13 retain progression and the performance, transfer and retention questions.
- **Learning-product practices:** may enact a selected explanation, task, feedback interaction, plan, or schedule for a declared audience; the product does not make the Method effective for a person by publication.

### HCD.5:End

## HCD.6 - Design Representative Practice Tasks

> **Type:** Human Capability Development practitioner practice-task design pattern
> **Status:** Stable

### HCD.6:0 - Use This When

Use this pattern when a named human contribution and a capability-development Method have been selected, but the person still needs a task in which to recognize the situation, act, obtain an inspectable result, receive feedback and improve the action. Begin with the target action and target-domain truth; do not begin by changing names, adding difficulty, or copying a production task without a learning purpose.

The first useful result is a **representative practice set**: a sufficiently whole task family with a worked demonstration or explanation where useful, a first attempt, repetitions or variations selected for the practice purpose, target-domain success and critical-error criteria, permitted help, feedback and correction opportunities, and progression or return conditions. The set states what each task is intended to expose. It does not establish that the tasks were performed or that capability changed.

The practical gain is an interpretable attempt. A practitioner can tell whether the person failed to calculate, to recognize the applicable Method, to challenge an unsupported source, to coordinate a specialist contribution, or to act when the supplied evidence is sufficient. A warranted refusal and a supported continuation can both be correct in different cases.

Do not use HCD.6 to invent target-domain correctness, turn a worked answer into learner evidence, schedule all repetitions, provide unavailable teachers or tools, or assess later capability. HCD.5 supplies the selected development Method; HCD.7–HCD.8 supply needed support; HCD.9–HCD.10 enact and vary practice; HCD.11–HCD.13 interpret performance, transfer, and retention.

When the practical question is how the person could move between different ways of acting, use the local model from HCD.4:4.2.1–4.3.1 or an equivalent qualified account. HCD.6 connects a proposed change to learning activities, help and observations, and can design alternative pathways through it. The model describes possibilities; the selected pathway plans opportunities; the learning trajectory records what was actually attempted and observed. A simple correction can still use one task without a larger progression model.

When learners can perform the preliminary actions but miss a relation in the next explanation, §4.2.2 connects preparation, explanation and a fresh application. §5.7 constructs both a learner-generated solution and a worked-solution alternative under explicit resource limits.

#### HCD.6:0.1 - Working Terms


| Name in this pattern | What it denotes |
| --- | --- |
| target human action | The recognition, judgement, operation, coordination, or result-producing contribution the person is intended to practise under stated conditions. |
| representative practice task | A bounded task that preserves the later-Work relations needed to elicit the target action and interpret its result. Representation is relative to the contribution and claim; visual realism or a workplace label is not enough. |
| sufficiently whole task | A task containing the purpose, result recipient, decision-bearing conditions, required contributions, interfaces, and stopping or critical-error boundaries needed for the target action. It may omit detail that does not change that action. |
| decision-bearing condition | A fact whose value can change which Method applies, which action is warranted, or which result can be supported. |
| worked explanation | A demonstration that exposes the intermediate observations, comparisons, reasons, checks, and uncertainty needed for the target action rather than showing only the final answer. |
| answer-bearing cue | Information that supplies the Method choice, decisive relation, calculation, or conclusion the current attempt is meant to elicit from the person. A legitimate reference or tool is not answer-bearing merely because it helps. |
| permitted help | The references, tools, AI actions, prompts, peers, specialists, teacher moves, and other support allowed for one stated practice purpose. It remains distinct from help actually available and help actually received. |
| representative practice set | The task descriptions, conditions, materials, permitted help, criteria, variations, feedback opportunities, progression or return rules, and evidence-purpose limits needed for a coherent practice use. |

A task description, learning product, performed attempt, work product, feedback event, and capability claim remain different objects. HCD.6 designs the task set; later Methods establish what was provided, performed, observed, and inferred.

### HCD.6:1 - Problem Frame

A practice task can look realistic while testing the wrong contribution. A pump story can reduce to arithmetic when the target is causal discrimination. A ticket-queue story can repeat the same calculation even though the real difficulty is choosing the unit of account. An engineering release case can reward generic caution when a complete compatible report actually supports a bounded action.

Support changes the task. A worked example may help a novice see the reasoning, but leaving the same intermediate prompts in the next attempt can turn recognition into copying. Removing every source or tool can make the task unlike later Work and test memory that was never required. AI assistance can generate a plausible answer while hiding whether the person noticed a configuration mismatch.

The practitioner therefore has to preserve the relations that make the target action necessary and choose help for the current practice purpose. When recognition or adaptation is the target, vary a condition that changes the warranted action rather than just the scenery.

### HCD.6:2 - Problem

The common shortcut is surface variation: change the industry, numbers, names, or diagram while leaving the same Method and answer obvious. Repetition may improve familiarity without showing whether the person can recognize applicability or adapt the Method.

The opposite shortcut maximizes authenticity. A full production case includes so many uncontrolled dependencies, missing inputs, risks, and specialist decisions that neither learner nor practitioner can tell which contribution changed. Complexity becomes noise rather than representation.

A third shortcut treats refusal as the safest universal answer. It can hide a real capability gap when sufficient evidence is present and action is required. The task set must include both missing-evidence and sufficient-evidence cases when the target contribution depends on that distinction.

### HCD.6:3 - Forces

- Whole tasks expose coordination and applicability, while irrelevant complexity can make the target action uninterpretable.
- Worked explanations can reveal reasoning, while answer-bearing cues can conceal recognition and selection.
- Legitimate references, AI, tools, and specialists belong to later Work, while their contributions must not be attributed to the person.
